lessons.title: Lección Primera
lessons.lede: The experiment begins here: Guillermo F. Hall Avilés’ course, a notebook, a microphone and a determination to discover whether Spanish can become something genuinely usable.
lessons.aim: Meet the first Spanish patterns through animals, size and direct questions
lessons.dayNote: Day 1. Excited. A little daunted. Why on earth did I challenge myself with this? Here goes… — A.W.P.G.
lessons.curiosityText: The first step is to read through Lección Primera in Guillermo F. Hall Avilés’ Poco a Poco.
lessons.curiositySample: El elefante es un animal. ¿Qué es el elefante? Es un animal.

studySteps.title: Write out the vocabulary
studySteps.text: Write each word in Spanish and English. Keep the two languages together so the vocabulary can be checked and recalled.

studySteps.title: Copy the lesson text by hand
studySteps.text: Copy the opening conversation from the book to become accustomed to forming and seeing the Spanish words.

studySteps.title: Think in plain English
studySteps.text: Record what the repeated forms and word order appear to be doing before reaching for a technical explanation.

studySteps.title: Complete Poco a Poco’s exercises
studySteps.text: Work from the original book. This site records the experience while following the textbook lesson.

checklist: Read Lección Primera in Poco a Poco
Make a genuine first reading before studying
Write the vocabulary in Spanish and English
Copy the lesson text by hand
Record what seemed easy, difficult or surprising
Return for a second reading after study
lessons.todayLatin: This first published lesson establishes the experiment: read, listen, notice, write, practise and return. The reader can use the same sequence and mark the lesson complete when finished.
